Surah 96 is Meccan.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

{1} This surah is the first of the Qur'anic surahs to be revealed to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), for it was revealed to him at the beginning of prophethood, when he did not know what the Book (al-kitab) or faith (al-iman) was. Jibril (peace be upon him) came to him with the message and commanded him to read, but he refused and said: "I am not one who reads!" Jibril kept at him until he read. Then Allah revealed: ﴿Read in the name of your Lord who created﴾, which is a general statement about all creation.

{2} Then He singled out man and mentioned the beginning of his creation: ﴿from a clinging substance﴾. The One who created man and took care to arrange his affairs must surely direct him by command and prohibition, and that is through sending messengers and revealing books. For this reason, after the command to read, He mentioned the creation of man.

{3–5} Then He said: ﴿Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous﴾; that is, He is abundant in attributes, vast in them, abundant in generosity and benevolence, and vast in bounty. From His generosity is that He taught all kinds of knowledge, and ﴿taught by the pen. He taught man that which he did not know﴾. For He, exalted is He, brought him forth from his mother's womb knowing nothing, and gave him hearing, sight and hearts, and facilitated for him the means of knowledge: He taught him the Qur'an, He taught him wisdom, and He taught him by the pen, [by which knowledge is preserved] and rights are secured, and which serves as messengers to people, standing in for their speech. So praise and blessing belong to Allah, who has bestowed these favours upon His servants, favours for which they cannot render adequate recompense or gratitude. Then He bestowed upon them wealth and abundance of provision.

{6–8} But man, because of his ignorance and wrongdoing, when he sees himself as rich, becomes insolent, transgresses, and tyrannises against guidance, and forgets that to his Lord is ﴿the return﴾; he does not fear the recompense. Indeed, his condition may reach the point where he abandons guidance himself and calls others to abandon it too, so he forbids prayer, which is the best of the acts of faith.

{9–14} Allah says to this rebellious, obstinate one: ﴿Have you considered﴾, O forbidder of the servant when he prays, ﴿if he is upon guidance﴾, that is, knowledge of the truth and acting upon it, ﴿or enjoins piety﴾ upon others. Is it fitting that one whose description is this should be forbidden? Is not his prohibition among the greatest acts of opposition to Allah and warfare against the truth? For prohibition is directed only at one who is himself not upon guidance, or who commands others contrary to piety. ﴿Have you considered if he denies﴾ the truth, forbidding it, ﴿and turns away﴾ from the command? Does he not fear Allah and dread His punishment? ﴿Does he not know that Allah sees﴾ what he does and commits?

{15–16} Then He threatens him if he persists in his condition, saying: ﴿No! If he does not cease﴾ from what he says and does, ﴿We will surely seize him by the forelock﴾; that is, We will seize his forelock with a violent grip, and it is deserving of this, for it is ﴿a lying, sinning forelock﴾; that is, lying in its speech and sinning in its deeds.

{17–18} ﴿Then let him call his associates﴾, that is, the people of his assembly, his companions and those around him, so that they may help him against what has befallen him. ﴿We will call the guards of Hell﴾, that is, the keepers of Hell, to seize him and punish him. Let him see which of the two parties is stronger and more capable. This is the state of the forbidder and the punishment with which he is threatened.

{19} As for the state of the one who is forbidden, Allah commanded him not to heed this forbidder and not to submit to his prohibition, saying: ﴿No! Do not obey him﴾; that is, he commands only what brings loss. ﴿And prostrate and draw near﴾ to your Lord: draw near to Him through prostration and other kinds of obedience and acts of nearness, for all of them bring one closer to His pleasure and nearer to Him. This applies generally to every forbidder of good and every one forbidden from it, although it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl when he forbade the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from prayer, and tormented and harmed him.

Finished. And praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
